contract: GET /hls/:stream/:file. Serve the live-session .m3u8 playlist and .ts segments of a transcoded session inside the stream directory without a bearer token, with the m3u8/mp2t MIME types, byte ranges and 400/404 rejections; a missing segment before the start offset restarts the transcode, and requests after close answer 404.
evidence: go-backend/testmachine/contracts/parity/full-suite-report.json#hls-playlist (historical differential lead; the packet scenarios above are the current execution)
exceptions: force is not applicable: the route has no force/refresh mode; every request derives its behaviour from the live stream state.

The accepted playback lifecycle packet's documented Go differences are not asserted here: upstream returns a 404 for a missing segment after completion, and the scenarios do not pin the reset retry timing.

invariants.contract: GET /hls/:stream/output.m3u8 of an open transcoded session answers 200 without a bearer token as application/vnd.apple.mpegurl with a VOD playlist (#EXTM3U, version 3, target duration 6, media sequence 0, end list) that lists output-0.ts through output-10.ts for The Beginning; GET of output-0.ts answers 200 as video/mp2t with Accept-Ranges: bytes, and the same request with the owner's token returns identical bytes. An AC3 (.mka) audiobook also transcodes and serves a 200 playlist and a non-empty first segment; the ffmpeg bitrate/channel options of Stream.js:278-283 are not externally observable and are not asserted.

GET /hls/:stream/:file answers 400 for a .txt file, the concat file and a ../ path outside the stream folder, and 404 for an unknown stream id; none of the rejected requests emits stream_reset or interrupts the live stream, which still serves its segment.

A repeated segment request returns identical bytes, a Range of bytes=1000-1999 answers 206 with Content-Range bytes 1000-1999/<size> and exactly those bytes, a range starting past the end answers 416 with Content-Range bytes */<size>, and a repeated playlist request returns the same body.

For a session started at 44 s the playlist still lists every segment from segment 0 while the transcode starts at segment 2; requesting the missing output-1.ts answers 404, broadcasts stream_reset {startTime: 6, streamId} to the watching owner and restarts the transcode from the beginning, after which output-0.ts and output-1.ts are served non-empty. (Requesting segment 0 instead returns a falsy start time and is silent, proven by INV-SOCKET-OUTGOING-STREAM-RESET-TRIGGER-001.)
After the playback session is closed the playlist and the segments of that stream answer 404 and the metadata/streams/<session id> folder has been removed.
